sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Off-Price Wholesale Liquidation of Branded Overstock Apparel

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified commercial law under the French Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1994, amended by 2006 protocol)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2008, amended by 2012 protocol)
France–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, amended by 2005 and 2010 protocols)
France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984, amended by 2007 protocol)
France–Canada Double Taxation Agreement (1975, amended by 2013 protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 through L.561-57-1, including Article L.561-2-2 (beneficial ownership threshold), and Articles L.561-45 through L.561-47 (UBO declaration); Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 transposing AMLD4, as amended; Décret n° 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017; Décret n° 2019-1192 of 20 November 2019; Regulation (EU) 2015/849, as amended; Tracfin AML guidance for the private sector; Code de commerce, Article L.123-1, R.123-1, and R.123-13.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport or national identity card of each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the country of origin's competent authority; non-Hague jurisdictions shall use Consular Legalization by the French Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, Chamber of Commerce, or Ministry of Justice in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the shareholder's jurisdiction is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization by the French Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation of the corporate shareholder's constitutional documents (articles of association, current directors, and UBO chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-certified translator in France or translator admitted to the equivalent foreign court system
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original constituting document must be apostilled or legalized; the translation is attached to that source and certified as true by the translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing source of funds and banking history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant credit institution holding the shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature of the issuing bank official notarized and apostilled/legalized where required by the French / EU bank's KYC process

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-pending criminal conviction / police clearance for each director and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal-record registry or police authority in the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, depending on the issuing state's status

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, statutory auditors, and material counterparties against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list when USD SWIFT wires are involved, the French national asset-freezing list administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor, and the French AML alerts on PEPs published by Tracfin. Enhanced due diligence applies under Articles L.561-10 to L.561-14 of the Code monétaire et financier. For off-price wholesale garment trading, customer and supplier UBO chains must be documented, source-of-funds narratives captured, and transaction timing cross-checked against dispatch and customs records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) national electronic portal; filing is submitted through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet unique operated with the INPI)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Latin/Roman characters. Non-Latin original names must be transliterated into Latin script in the articles of association and in the RCS record. The legal form suffix 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or 'SAS' is mandatory. French legal documents must be drafted in French, and the registry will not accept a name contrary to public order, deceptive, or confusingly similar to a protected existing mark or corporate enterprise name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank – requires prior prudential authorization from ACPR and an EU banking licence
Assurance / Insurance – reserved for regulated insurance undertakings supervised by ACPR
Pharmacie – reserved for holders of a pharmacy licence
République / National / Nation – generally prohibited without ministerial authorization because it falsely implies official state status
Préfecture / Ministère / Gouvernement – requires prior ministerial authorization; strongly disfavoured for private commercial entities
Tribunal / Chambre de commerce / Greffe – implies judicial or official registry status and is prohibited for private companies
Bourse / Exchange – may imply regulated financial-market activity and may trigger financial-market authority approval or rejection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS registry does not issue a statutory name reservation, but a preliminary 'certificat de non-opposition' may be requested with the draft articles. On rejection, the applicant must request written reasons from the greffe. The applicant may first file a hierarchical appeal (recours gracieux) with the president of the competent commercial court. If refused or unanswered, a judicial appeal must be filed within 15 days of notification by 'requête simple' before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce or the delegated judge responsible for registry supervision, attaching the rejected name dossier, proposed articles, and evidence of distinctiveness. For trademark-based objections, a civil action may be brought in the Tribunal Judiciaire.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a wholesale apparel-liquidation SAS, provided the domiciliation service holds an approved commercial lease or administrative authorization and a written domiciliation contract is executed. The registered office address will appear in the RCS. The arrangement is not a substitute for substantive local presence and may increase scrutiny by the tax administration, especially where non-resident UBOs hold effective management outside France. French law limits continuous domiciliation at a given virtual office location and requires notification to the registry; a physical warehouse or sales office is recommended to satisfy commercial-substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. For an established non-licensed trader, the annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the French DREETS or anti-VAT-fraud body (DNED) is estimated at 5–10% in the baseline scenario. It rises to 15–25% when UBOs are non-resident, when the warehouse is used for stock holding, or where customs / VAT filings show inconsistencies in off-price garment flows.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS (Registre du commerce et des sociétés) incorporation filing fee, including M0/M1/M2 registration forms and UBO declaration intake
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe of the competent Tribunal de Commerce / RCS portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated court fee (frais de greffe) under applicable French tariff schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in an approved journal d'annonces légales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated per-line tariff for legal announcements (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and execution of the French-language SAS articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Avocat or, where used, a French Notaire
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for French corporate counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign shareholder identity, constitutional, and good-standing documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) or court-recognized translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Sworn translation market tariff, usually EUR 35–60 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the foreign documents in the mandatory bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent ministry / Secretary of State of the foreign issuing state and, when required, the French Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign statutory apostille fees plus French consular legalization tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement for one year (virtual or leased office address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved French corporate domiciliation service (boutique de domiciliation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark, typically EUR 30–80 per month plus setup fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening and AML/KYC administration fee for a non-resident commercial account supporting SWIFT Wire and ACH/SEPA rails
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French or EU licensed banking institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for non-resident corporate account opening, market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) contingency for post-incorporation threshold tests
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commissaire aux comptes registered with the French National Audit Body
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory contingency; not required at incorporation because the SAS does not yet exceed the Code de commerce thresholds

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. governing commercial registration; Articles L.561-46 et seq. governing beneficial ownership declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration recorded in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a legal entity (formalité de création) submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, together with the signed SAS articles of association and the declaration of beneficial owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The amount is freely determined in the articles of association. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid on incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must generally be fully contributed at incorporation. Funds may be deposited with a bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the deposit certificate is required for registration. The stated amount excludes the separate beneficial-owner filing fee, legal-notice publication cost, and professional fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President noted that the Company had been duly incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée and that the subscribed share capital had been deposited in accordance with applicable law. It was resolved that the Company accept and record the subscriptions and payments described in the subscription schedule, adopt the registered office at the address stated in the articles of association, and approve the opening and operation of the Company’s bank accounts. It was further resolved to appoint [Name] as President for an unlimited term, with authority to represent the Company, and [Name], if applicable, as Directeur Général.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate particulars and reserve the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique portal and, where applicable, the commercial premises landlord or domiciliation provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the proposed name, corporate purpose, share capital, share classes, governance rules, financial year, registered office, President, and any Directeur Général. Obtain a valid lease, domiciliation agreement, or registered-office hosting certificate. Verify that the premises permit the intended wholesale and storage activities.
required_dossiers: Registered-office title, lease, or domiciliation certificate
Identification documents for shareholders and officers
Foreign shareholder or officer corporate documents, if applicable
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the address or purpose before filing; replace non-compliant domiciliation evidence; obtain written landlord consent where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and, where applicable, a French notary or qualified legal adviser
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the articles of association in French or with an accurate French version. Specify the share capital, contribution terms, transfer restrictions, decision-making procedures, President’s powers, approval rights, financial year, and dissolution provisions. Execute electronically only where the signature method reliably identifies the signatories and preserves document integrity.
required_dossiers: Special approval or power of attorney documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend, re-execute, or notarize defective articles; obtain missing signatures and correct inconsistencies between the articles and filing data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the capital deposit account and obtain the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed articles, draft registration documents, identification and anti-money-laundering materials, subscription schedule, and evidence of the registered office. Deposit at least 50% of cash contributions. Obtain the certificate of deposit and retain the deposit account documentation for release after registration.
required_dossiers: Identity and address evidence for subscribers and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC queries, provide certified translations or apostilles, replace incomplete documents, and use a notarial or Caisse des Dépôts deposit route if the bank declines onboarding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal for Legal Announcements (journal d’annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, President, and registration details as applicable. Obtain the publication certificate. Use the regulated format and current departmental tariff.
required_dossiers: Signed articles or incorporation information sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice or rectification publication if the announcement contains an error; retain both the original and corrective certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the electronic incorporation and beneficial-owner filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for business formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online creation formalité, upload the signed articles, capital deposit certificate, legal-notice publication certificate, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, identification documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. State the appropriate activity for wholesale apparel trading and any warehouse activity. Pay the applicable registration and beneficial-owner charges and electronically sign the filing.
required_dossiers: President declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Corporate subscriber documents and powers of attorney
Certified French translations and apostilles, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard, answer requests for regularization within the stated deadline, replace unreadable or uncertified documents, and resubmit corrected forms without changing the filing date where the portal permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and release the capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry and the capital-deposit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm issuance of the SIREN, SIRET, APE code, and Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence. Provide the registration evidence to the deposit institution to unlock the capital account. Maintain the company’s statutory registers, beneficial-owner records, accounting records, and corporate approvals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a registry correction request for inaccurate company data; escalate unresolved procedural issues to the competent greffe or use the INPI support and regularization channels.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement post-incorporation governance and operating compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company President, shareholders, tax administration, customs administration, and applicable labor authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board or shareholder resolutions, confirm officer mandates, activate accounting and invoicing systems, register for applicable VAT obligations, assess EORI and customs requirements for imports or exports, and implement workplace, product, traceability, and consumer-law controls. Verify whether the warehouse triggers any premises-specific regulatory regime.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or customs registrations, submit missing declarations, notify changes to the registry, and obtain specialist advice before commencing regulated storage, construction, or employment activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ordinary off-price wholesale trading of finished garments. For premises or storage activities potentially falling under an environmental classification, the competent authority is the relevant Préfecture and its regional environmental directorate, Direction Régionale de l’Environnement, de l’Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating licence is required for ordinary wholesale trading of finished garments. A premises-specific authorization, declaration, or registration may be required if the warehouse falls within a classified installation regime under the French nomenclature des installations classées pour la protection de l’environnement (ICPE).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, with examination by the competent Préfecture and DREAL; environmental-authority review may be performed by the Conseil général de l’environnement et du développement durable or the competent regional environmental authority, depending on the project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally Exempt or outside EIA requirements for ordinary wholesale garment premises with no manufacturing, significant emissions, or regulated hazardous storage. A case-specific ICPE and environmental-impact screening is required for large warehouses, substantial combustible-material storage, construction projects, or other classified activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine process wastewater or VOC limit normally applies to pure garment wholesale operations. The company must prevent uncontrolled releases, comply with applicable municipal wastewater rules, manage packaging and business waste through authorized channels, maintain fire-prevention controls for combustible textile stock, and comply with any site-specific ICPE, wastewater, air-emission, or hazardous-waste requirements imposed by the Préfecture.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain premises fire-safety documentation and maintain accessible emergency exits, extinguishers, alarm systems, emergency lighting, evacuation plans, and periodic inspections. If the premises are open to the public, comply with établissement recevant du public rules and obtain the required safety opinion or authorization. Verify structural floor-load capacity for garment storage and racking, secure racking against collapse, perform electrical and equipment inspections, prepare the required workplace risk assessment document (document unique d’évaluation des risques professionnels), and provide occupational safety training. No separate general occupational operating clearance is normally required for an ordinary wholesale warehouse.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - National tax authority; official portals: impots.gouv.fr and Douane.gouv.fr (customs/VAT on imports/exports)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain a French SIREN/SIRET and Tax ID (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) by filing Form 331A (Cerfa 11984) with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the French tax representative or permanent establishment. For remote sellers, simplified electronic VAT registration via impots.gouv.fr is available; an EORI number must also be obtained through pro.douane.gov.fr for customs operations. The registration is effective immediately and a French VAT ID is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. A newly created SAS may elect for up to 5 fiscal years to be treated as pass-through (assujettie à l'impôt sur le revenu) under CGI Art. 239 bis AA, provided it files the option before the end of the third month after incorporation and satisfies the SME and ownership tests. Alternatively, certain qualifying SASs may irrevocably elect corporate income tax treatment under CGI Art. 206. Group VAT and corporate income tax elections are available under French organic tax law for established groups. Anti-hybrid rules under EU ATAD and CGI Art. 212 bis / 214 ter restrict mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established foreign entities making taxable supplies in France; a mandatory French VAT registration is triggered from the first taxable transaction. For domestic small businesses the annual turnover exemption is EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services. The EU distance-selling threshold of EUR 35,000 applies to intra-Community remote sales to French consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G e-invoices must be submitted through the Chorus Pro portal using Factur-X formats. Mandatory B2B e-invoicing is phased-in from 1 September 2026 for large taxpayers and 1 September 2027 for all taxable persons; e-reporting of transaction data (B2B cross-border and B2C sales) is required via certified API infrastructure. France, however, does not operate a general real-time fiscal clearance/stamping regime for wholesale trading; retail cash receipts require approved fiscal memory software or a certified fiscal till system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from France to a destination outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT where the exporter retains proof of physical dispatch and the export entry information, and the goods leave the EU by way of a customs formality (EX-E electronic declaration or paper DAU). Intra-Community supplies of goods to another EU member state are zero-rated if the customer holds a valid EU VAT ID and the EC-sales list and INTRASTAT are filed. Services directly related to exported goods, or rendered to a non-EU customer, where the place of supply is outside the EU, are also zero-rated; otherwise an exemption may require evidence that the customer is established outside the EU and the service is actually used outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / CMR / Airway Bill as the proof of transport
Inward Remittance Certificate (Attestation de domiciliation bancaire) or bank proof of foreign-exchange repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities may retroactively reclaim zero-rated VAT where export evidence is deficient, supported by a penalty of 40% for lack of good faith (défaut de bonne foi) or 80% for abusive/manifestly false declarations (CGI Art. 1729). Monthly late-payment interest accrues at 0.55% per month. Customs false export declarations carry a separate penalty under the Code des Douanes (Art. 413-14) of up to EUR 750,000 and a potential jail term; repeat or organised fraud reduces all VAT and customs reliefs and triggers full clawback plus interest and sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), acting within the Eurosystem and under the legal framework of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) and relevant EU regulations; foreign exchange and cross-border financial relations are jointly administered by the Banque de France and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) for balance-of-payments statistics and inward investment declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible and the current account is free from exchange control restrictions. Capital account transactions are likewise open, with no prior authorization required for ordinary commercial wholesale activities such as finished-garments liquidation trading. Profit remittances to non-residents are permitted free of any foreign exchange control barrier, subject only to French withholding tax on dividends or interest unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary/Interest and Royalties Directives. Non-resident shareholders must however observe French fiscal and administrative declarations, including Banque de France outward payment reporting for direct investment transactions. No restrictions apply to invoicing or settling off-price apparel imports and exports in EUR, USD, or other freely convertible currencies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory mandatory surrender or conversion ratio for export proceeds for French-resident entities. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in domestic or foreign-currency accounts. Nevertheless, all export proceeds must be promptly repatriated to a French/EU bank account for corporate treasury control, and the company must maintain supporting invoices, customs declarations, and bank records for six years for French tax and customs audits. For balance-of-payments statistical purposes, Banque de France may require monthly reporting of cross-border settlements above the applicable threshold, but no conversion obligation exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance and LC Lines
Operational Account / USD Clearing and FX Hedging

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material constraints. Licensed Electronic Money Institutions in France (e.g., Qonto, Shine, N26) can open a French EUR IBAN for a SAS quickly through fully remote onboarding, which is operationally agile for day-to-day EUR receipts and supplier payments. However, EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot provide documentary letters of credit, trade finance limits, or committed cross-border foreign-exchange hedging facilities. They also may reject complex liquidation wholesaler flows where many beneficiary countries and USD wires are involved. EMIs should therefore be treated as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail only; the primary treasury account and capital escrow should be held with a tier-1 French banking institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SAS with non-resident shareholders or directors, French banks commonly require at least one legal representative (Président or Directeur Général) to attend a physical or live video-interview KYC meeting. Remote opening is increasingly possible when all documentation is digitized and notarized, but physical branch presence dramatically improves viability at BNP Paribas, Société Générale, and Crédit Agricole. The bank will apply the French AML/CFT obligations issued by ACPR, and the UBO (bénéficiaire effectif) declarations must match the RNE (Registre National des Entreprises) filing. Legalization or apostille of non-French corporate documents and ID is mandatory for all non-EU UBOs, and a sworn translation into French is typically required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owner located in a tax-haven or FATF grey-listed jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports, apostilled/legalized corporate registry abstracts, bank references from the UBO's primary bank, source-of-wealth documentation including tax returns and audited financial statements, notarized shareholder register, UBO declaration filed in France, FSMA/FATF-compliant risk assessment, and a commercial rationale letter describing the SAS's actual activities in France and the EU.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, multi-country disbursements to numerous apparel suppliers and liquidation intermediaries inconsistent with the entity's short history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed wholesale and consignment contracts, warehouse leases, inventory reconciliation reports, original supplier invoices with HS/ISIC codes, bill of lading and customs entry evidence, pro-forma transaction-flow diagram, the company's AML risk self-assessment, board resolution approving treasury limits, and an external auditor's letter confirming negative pledge and beneficial ownership of the goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions with counterparties in countries flagged for sanctions or high-money-laundering risk, especially in secondary apparel export territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full sanctions/PEP screening results of every counterparty, completed KYC pack for each buyer and seller, OECD and French customs no-circumvention declarations, end-customer attestations, eligibility certificates for excluded goods, ISBP/ICC trade documents (LC, packing list, certificate of origin), and a contractual undertaking prohibiting re-export to embargoed countries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the SAS's registered business scope and the expected turnover volume of off-price apparel liquidation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated RNE/RCS registration reflecting wholesale of apparel under ISIC 4641, SIREN/SIRET codes, VAT registration certificate, EORI number, projected financial statements for 24 months, stock-in-trade valuation reports from registered appraisers, and bank reference letters from the group's long-tenured operating entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through the receiving French bank's clearing channel. The payment must clearly indicate the French SAS SIREN number and purpose using Banque de France's international transaction nomenclature (direct investment purpose code for capital increases, or loan purpose code for shareholder advances). Non-EU investors must file the statutory direct foreign investment declaration with Banque de France after the operation, unless the sector is strategic and requires prior authorization; finished-garments wholesale is not a regulated sensitive sector. A compliance-ready package should include the board/shareholder resolution approving the capital contribution, the notarized or certified copy of the share issuance deed, source-of-funds documentation, and the updated RNE extract. If the capital is injected as a shareholder loan, a formal loan agreement with commercial terms, ISIN/purpose label, and French tax entity reporting is required. The receiving bank will verify OBO (ordering bank) and BIC validations and may request six months of source-account statements for AML purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements to suppliers and third-party liquidators, the preferred clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for high-value cross-border USD/EUR wires; (2) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments to EU counterparties; (3) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for urgent disbursements; (4) Commercial letters of credit issued by the tier-1 French bank under UCP600, because off-price apparel liquidation frequently requires documentary protection against title disputes; and (5) trade collection (documents against payment) for smaller recurring purchases. The SAS should maintain a dedicated USD correspondent account at a French clearing bank with access to the U.S. Fedwire system if paying U.S. vendors, while flows to Southeast Asian and South Asian suppliers may be routed through EUR-USD cover payments. All outbound wires must include precise item descriptions, HS codes, customs invoice numbers, and the French exporter reference to satisfy both the bank's transaction monitoring and the French customs authorities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forwards with maturity up to 12 months under ISDA or French FBF master agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked by a French licensed credit institution, permitted for hedging restricted-currency receivables when settlement in non-convertible currency is impossible
Currency swaps (FX swaps) combining spot and forward legs for managing short-term liquidity in USD, GBP, and CNY if the bank approves a trading line
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP options purchased for downside protection on liquidation receivables
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps solely when the SAS has an underlying cross-border debt facility, not for speculative purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) at RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end for shareholder approval, plus 1 month for deposit; maximum 7 months after year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: fine up to EUR 1,500 for natural persons and EUR 4,500 for the company; repeated default may trigger a court injunction and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration annuelle de confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the anniversary of the company's RCS registration; a simple confirmation suffices if no UBO data has changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update UBO data: up to 6 months imprisonment and EUR 30,000 fine per individual; EUR 150,000 fine for the company; possible RCS strike-off after repeated failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats n° 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: file electronically by 3 May of the following year; for other year-ends: within 3 months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: automatic 10% surcharge on the assessed corporate income tax (minimum EUR 100), late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, and an additional 5% penalty if payment is not made within 30 days; deliberate omissions can lead to higher penalties and administrative tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business property tax declaration (cotisation foncière des entreprises – CFE, form 1447-C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – local business tax office (service des impôts des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the date shown on the DGFiP notice; generally 31 December for existing businesses; for new activities, filing within 30 days after commencement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing: penalty ranging from 5% to 40% of assessed CFE depending on severity; late payment accrues monthly interest at 0.20%; persistent non-payment may lead to enforced collection but does not directly cause RCS strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (commissaire aux comptes) when at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded at year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 5,000,000; net turnover > EUR 10,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Group-structured SAS may also be subject to audit under consolidation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French local GAAP (PCG) governed by ANC Regulation No. 2014-03; IFRS applies only for consolidated financial statements of listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, within 30 days of the RCS registration anniversary, the SAS must file a confirmation that the list of ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) remains unchanged. Any share transfer that changes a 25% ownership or voting threshold requires an updated UBO declaration to be filed within 15 days of the transfer; the transfer itself must be written into the mandatory securities-movement ledger.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (share issue and transfer register)
Registre des décisions des associés / procès-verbaux (shareholder minutes and decisions book)
Registre de nantissement des actions (share pledge and security register)
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO declaration supporting file)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 1,800 per annum (typical legal and administrative domiciliation at a CPA, registered agent, or corporate services provider)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 20,000 per annum (typical certified audit fee for a small-to-mid-size French SAS; amount rises with turnover, group complexity, and internal-control scope)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate applicable to fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2022; reduced from 26.5% in 2021, 28% in 2020 and 33.33% before 2018)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10M); Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100M and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs on eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; no sector-specific tax holiday for wholesale garment liquidation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (French law allows indefinite loss carryforward; annual deduction capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; carryback limited to one year and EUR 1,000,000)
